newsitem.title: USA: CBOE's move to split OEX gains momentum - sources.
newsitem.headline: CBOE's move to split OEX gains momentum - sources.

text.p: A move by the Chicago Board Options Exchange to halve the size of its bellwether stock index option, the Standard & Poor's 100 index, is gathering steam, industry sources said.
"There's talk going around again that we're going to split the OEX," one index options dealer said.
CBOE officials were not available for comment.
Exchange sources said one key committee examining a split of the OEX was scheduled to meet on Monday.
"It's getting more momentum in a majority of quarters," one exchange source said. "We have many committees to clear.
"It hasn't gotten to the final step yet," he said.
In early March, the exchange said it was considering cutting the size of the OEX in half to lower premiums and help boost volumes.
At the time, exchange sources said the committee that oversees OEX procedures had decided to consider a split at a later date rather than endorse the idea outright.

In May, exchange chairman and chief executive William Brodsky told Reuters the plan had been put on the back burner as the exchange threw its resources behind its bid to win the licensing of derivatives on Dow Jones & Co indexes.
The exchange won licenses to trade options on the Dow industrial average, Dow transportation average and Dow utility average in early June.
On Monday, the OEX ended at 896.53, up 2.94 points.
